cases.request: According to the current print preparation log, how many minutes should each print dry before stacking?

sources.text: Print preparation log. The proposed print comparison uses two sheets from the same paper batch and the same ink set. Place each sheet on a clean flat rack after printing. Keep the room ventilation and paper orientation consistent. The worktable should hold only the sheets, the rack and the observation form during preparation. Label the back of each sheet before printing so that marks cannot disturb the printed surface afterward. The observation form records the sheet label, paper batch and the time each sheet leaves the printer. Inspect the rack for dust and ensure that both sheets can lie flat without touching one another. Keep unused paper in its sleeve and return the sleeve to the cabinet before beginning the comparison. The current checklist below describes the approved handling procedure rather than any measured image-quality result. Drying interval: allow each print to dry for 12 minutes before stacking it. This interval replaces the earlier draft; use this current log when planning the schedule. After the session, store the observation forms with the labelled sample sheets and clean the worktable. No completed comparison or image-quality conclusions have been entered in this log.
